speaker: Doctor
text:
How long have you had this painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg, and does it have a history of trauma or insect bites?

REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count (CBC)
REQUEST TEST: Blood glucose level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: WBC: Normal, Hemoglobin: Normal, Platelets: Normal; Random Blood Glucose: Elevated

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Patient
text: No additional systemic symptoms mentioned. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your provider suggested cellulitis, but you describe an ulcerative lesion which is distinct from a simple infection, can you tell me exactly what the ulcer looks like—is the base red and granulating, or is it covered by a necrotic slough or a black eschar? Also, does the wound have a "punched-out" appearance with rolled edges?

REQUEST TEST: Wound Culture and Sensitivity
REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up clinical photo of the ulcer showing base characteristics and margins.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming the normal blood work; that makes an infectious etiology like typical cellulitis less likely. Given the "punched-out" appearance you described, could you tell me if this ulcer has been present on this specific spot for more than three weeks? Also, does your leg have a history of varicose veins or venous insufficiency?

REQUEST TEST: Venous Doppler Ultrasound
REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of ulcer edge and base

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Venous Doppler Ultrasound: Bilateral dilated tortuous veins noted; no acute thrombosis identified; history of varicose veins and venous insufficiency confirmed. Biopsy of ulcer edge and base: Histopathology shows neutrophilic infiltration without evidence of infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The combination of a punched-out ulcer with a violaceous border, negative infectious workup, and histopathology showing neutrophilic infiltration without organisms confirms this diagnosis of a neutrophilic dermatosis, which is often associated with venous insufficiency in your case.
